title: Fixed point in the redirect loop
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $b$ be a bit, and form the machine that redirects halting computations whose last output bit is not $b$ to a loop state. For any input $x$, any configuration $c$ of this redirected machine whose state is the loop state, and any $t \in \mathbb{N}$, running the machine for $t$ steps from $c$ returns $c$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-state Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet
A configuration $c$ of the redirected machine
The state of $c$ is the loop state
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and $b$ a bit, and
consider the halt-redirected machine of $M$ and $b$, which simulates $M$ silently while
recording the last bit $M$ has emitted, halts when $M$ halts with that bit equal to $b$,
and otherwise enters a loop state $\ell$. For every configuration $c$ of the
halt-redirected machine on an input $x$ whose control state is $\ell$, and every
$t \in \mathbb{N}$, running the halt-redirected machine for $t$ steps from $c$ returns
exactly $c$.
